stem_bark.text: The bark of Millingtonia hortensis is yellowish brown-coloured, thick and corky, longitudinally fissured and transversally cracked.
stem_bark.text_html: The bark of Millingtonia hortensis is yellowish brown-coloured, thick and corky, longitudinally fissured and transversally cracked.

flower.text: The flowers of Millingtonia hortensis are grouped in corymbose panicles. The calyx-tube is cup-shaped with 5 recurved and short lobes. The calyx is light green and 3 mm long and wide. The corolla is composed of a long tube (6-8 cm long and 2-3 mm across) and 5 lobes. The 5 corolla-lobes are ovate-elliptic, 1.5 cm long and 6-7 mm wide. The androecium is composed of 4 stamens. The filaments are 4 or 6 mm long and connate into a 3 mm long tube with ovoid anthers borne on the free tips of the filaments. The pistil is about 8 cm long. The flowers are very fragrant.
flower.text_html:
The flowers of Millingtonia hortensis are grouped in corymbose panicles.
The calyx-tube is cup-shaped with 5 recurved and short lobes. The calyx is light green and 3 mm long and wide.
The corolla is composed of a long tube (6-8 cm long and 2-3 mm across) and 5 lobes. The 5 corolla-lobes are ovate-elliptic, 1.5 cm long and 6-7 mm wide.
The androecium is composed of 4 stamens. The filaments are 4 or 6 mm long and connate into a 3 mm long tube with ovoid anthers borne on the free tips of the filaments.
The pistil is about 8 cm long.
The flowers are very fragrant.

leaf.text: The leaves of Millingtonia hortensis grow alternately on the stem (spirally arranged). The leaf is compound (bi-imparipinnate). The leaflets are bright green-coloured above and paler beneath. The leaflets are chartaceous and glabrous on both sides. The leaflets have a 2-3 mm long petiole . The leaflets of Millingtonia hortensis are 4-7 cm long and 2-3 cm wide. The shape of the blade is ovate, the apex is acuminate, the base is oblique and the margins are dentate-crenate. The venation of the leaf is reticulate with a prominent midrib.

habit.text: Millingtonia hortensis is a thornless, medium-sized and deciduous tree growing up to 12-15 m high.
habit.text_html: Millingtonia hortensis is a thornless, medium-sized and deciduous tree growing up to 12-15 m high.

ecology.text: In India, Millingtonia hortensis is used in roadside plantings and in parks.

distribution.text: Millingtonia hortensis is native to South Asia and South East Asia. The species is cultivated in most parts of India.
distribution.text_html:
• Distribution :

    Millingtonia hortensis is native to South Asia and South East Asia. The species is cultivated in most parts of India.

reproduction_dispersal.text: Millingtonia hortensis is bisexual (each flower of each individual has both male and female structures). Millingtonia hortensis is pollinated by a wide variety of insects and by sunbirds (in India). Mechanical dispersal : barochory (dispersal of seeds by gravity), self-propagation. The seeds disperse from the pods and germinate on sites with favourable conditions : the ripe dry fruits burst and scatter the seeds.
reproduction_dispersal.text_html:
• Sex distribution :

    Millingtonia hortensis is bisexual (each flower of each individual has both male and female structures).

  • Mode of pollination :

    Millingtonia hortensis is pollinated by a wide variety of insects and by sunbirds (in India).

  • Seed dispersal :

    Mechanical dispersal : barochory (dispersal of seeds by gravity), self-propagation.
    The seeds disperse from the pods and germinate on sites with favourable conditions : the ripe dry fruits burst and scatter the seeds.

others.text: Millingtonia hortensis is cultivated in gardens and avenues for its shade and beautiful and fragrant flowers.

handicrafts.text: The wood of Millingtonia hortensis is used as timber . The bark is used as an inferior substitute for cork . The leaves are also used as a cheap substitute for tobacco in cigarettes. Source : Wikipedia (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Millingtonia)

medicinal.text: The crushed leaves are used on skin diseases. The root decoction is drunk to treat malaria. The bark decoction is used to cure typhoid and as antipyretic. The flowers are used to treat asthma and sinusitis. Sources : - Khare, 2007, Indian Medicinal Plants, An Illustrated Dictionary - Quattrocchi, 2012, CRC World Dictionary of Medicinal and Poisonous Plants

reforestation.text: Millingtonia hortensis prefers full sun but can tolerate the half shade. It is drought resistant and it will grow in a wide variety of situations and soils but all soils need to be free draining. The species is propagated by seeds or by cuttings. 24 hours of soaking in water accelerates the germination process.
reforestation.text_html:
• Planting advice and requirements :

    Millingtonia hortensis prefers full sun but can tolerate the half shade. It is drought resistant and it will grow in a wide variety of situations and soils but all soils need to be free draining.
    The species is propagated by seeds or by cuttings.

  • Seed treatments :

    24 hours of soaking in water accelerates the germination process.
